subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Coffee Nap
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Coffee Nap usable.

hook.text: Drink coffee and immediately nap for 20 minutes. You'll wake up more alert than either alone would provide.

buildup.text: Sleep naturally clears adenosine from receptors. Caffeine takes 20 minutes to absorb into the brain.

discovery.text: By napping during the absorption window, you clear adenosine while caffeine moves in to block the empty receptors.

twist.text: Studies show coffee naps improve performance on driving and cognitive tests more than coffee or naps separately.

climax.text: The key is keeping the nap under 20 minutes—longer and you enter deep sleep, causing grogginess instead.

punchline.text: Coffee plus a 20-minute nap. Science's best alertness trick.

quiz.question: Why does a coffee nap work?
options: Sleep clears adenosine while caffeine absorbs to block the empty receptors
The heat from coffee relaxes you

details.summary: A coffee nap involves drinking coffee immediately before a 15 to 20 minute nap. During sleep, adenosine clears naturally from receptors, and when you wake, the caffeine has arrived to block any remaining ones. Studies show this combination outperforms either coffee or napping alone.
details.whyItMatters: The coffee nap is a surprisingly effective fatigue management technique backed by research. It leverages both biology and timing for maximum alertness recovery.
takeaways: Drink coffee then nap for 15 to 20 minutes for best results
Sleep clears adenosine while caffeine moves into position
Studies show it improves alertness more than coffee or naps alone

faq.question: Why does drinking coffee before a nap work better than after?
faq.answer: Caffeine takes 15 to 20 minutes to absorb and reach the brain. Timing it before the nap means it arrives just as you wake up, while the nap itself clears accumulated adenosine, giving caffeine a clean playing field.

faq.question: What happens if you sleep longer than 20 minutes during a coffee nap?
faq.answer: Sleeping longer risks entering deep sleep stages, which makes waking groggy, a phenomenon called sleep inertia. Keeping the nap to 15 to 20 minutes ensures you stay in light sleep and wake feeling refreshed.
